vitamin d.t: CONTRAINDICATIONS Calcitriol capsules should not be given to patients with hypercalcemia or evidence of vitamin D toxicity.

Since calcitriol is the most potent active metabolite of vitamin D 3 , pharmacological doses of vitamin D and its derivatives should be withheld during treatment with calcitriol to avoid possible additive effects and hypercalcemia (see WARNINGS ).

phenobarbital.t: The coadministration of phenytoin or phenobarbital will not affect plasma concentrations of calcitriol, but may reduce endogenous plasma levels of 25(OH)D 3 by accelerating metabolism.

phenytoin.t: The coadministration of phenytoin or phenobarbital will not affect plasma concentrations of calcitriol, but may reduce endogenous plasma levels of 25(OH)D 3 by accelerating metabolism.

ketoconazole.t: Reductions in serum endogenous calcitriol concentrations have been observed following the administration of 300 mg/day to 1200 mg/day ketoconazole for a week to healthy men.
Ketoconazole may inhibit both synthetic and catabolic enzymes of calcitriol.

thiazide.t: Thiazides are known to induce hypercalcemia by the reduction of calcium excretion in urine.
Some reports have shown that the concomitant administration of thiazides with calcitriol causes hypercalcemia.

cortico.t: A relationship of functional antagonism exists between vitamin D analogues, which promote calcium absorption, and corticosteroids, which inhibit calcium absorption.

antacid.t: Magnesium-containing preparations (e.g., antacids) and calcitriol should not be used concomitantly in patients on chronic renal dialysis because such use may lead to the development of hypermagnesemia.
Magnesium-containing preparations (e.g., antacids) may cause hypermagnesemia and should therefore not be taken during therapy with calcitriol by patients on chronic renal dialysis.
